Epidemiology and Endemic Regions: Tropical and subtropical regions of Asia, Africa and Latin America
Eurasia, Africa, Australia, Oceania; primarily reported from West Russia ("Karelian fever"), Finland ("Pogosta disease"), and Sweden ("Ockelbo disease")
Occurrence and Number of Reported Cases: Geographically most widely distributed alphavirus (lack of data on human cases) Karelian fever: rare (no data) Pogosta disease: ~140 cases (range 1-1282)/year Ockelbo disease: ~30 cases/year

Epidemiology and Endemic Regions: Australia, Papua New Guinea, West Papua
Occurrence and Number of Reported Cases: ~5000 cases per year in Australia; in 1979-1980 an epidemic with >60000 cases hit some pacific islands (New Caledonia, Fiji, Samoa, Cook Islands)

Frequency of Main Symptoms (%): Fever: 50 Rash: 40-60 Myalgia: 50-80 Arthralgia or arthritis: 70-95

Epidemiology and Endemic Regions: South America, primarily the Amazonian rainforest, Caribbean
Occurrence and Number of Reported Cases: Sporadic single cases and small outbreaks (involving ~10-100 cases)
